## Which firms should you shortlist by platform?

| Your environment or requirement | Companies to prioritize |
|--------|--------|
| AWS S3, Glue, Athena, cloud-native data lake | ClearScale, Accenture |
| Azure, Microsoft Fabric, enterprise governance | Deloitte, Accenture, NTT DATA |
| Databricks, Delta Lake, lakehouse architecture | Tredence, Slalom, Tiger Analytics |
| Hadoop or legacy big data migration | Cloudwick, NTT DATA, Accenture |
| AI/ML and advanced analytics on lake data | Tiger Analytics, Tredence |
| Large, multi-cloud enterprise transformation | Accenture, Deloitte, NTT DATA |
| Hands-on implementation with internal team collaboration | Slalom |


These are initial-fit recommendations, not verified exclusive platform specializations. Confirm each firm's current certifications and relevant project references before selecting a partner. [decisionminds.com](https://decisionminds.com/articles/best-data-engineering-consulting-firms-us-2026-guide?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[findalternatives.net](https://findalternatives.net/directory/data-lake-consulting-companies?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[dataengineeringcompanies.com](https://dataengineeringcompanies.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What to evaluate before hiring

I recommend scoring each shortlisted firm against these six criteria\:

- **Architecture\:** Can it design a scalable data lake or lakehouse using appropriate technologies such as Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or cloud-native storage?
- **Implementation experience\:** Can it demonstrate production deployments comparable to your data volume and complexity?
- **Governance and security\:** Does it cover access controls, lineage, metadata catalogs, retention, and compliance?
- **Cost optimization\:** Can it explain storage, compute, ingestion, and query costs?
- **AI readiness\:** Can the architecture support analytics, machine learning, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) where needed?
- **Delivery model\:** Will it deliver a working platform, documentation, knowledge transfer, and ongoing support?

Ask for two or three comparable client references and a clearly scoped proof of concept before committing to a large implementation.

## What to evaluate before hiring

I recommend scoring each shortlisted firm against these six criteria\:

- **Architecture\:** Can it design a scalable data lake or lakehouse using appropriate technologies such as Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, or cloud-native storage?
- **Implementation experience\:** Can it demonstrate production deployments comparable to your data volume and complexity?
- **Governance and security\:** Does it cover access controls, lineage, metadata catalogs, retention, and compliance?
- **Cost optimization\:** Can it explain storage, compute, ingestion, and query costs?
- **AI readiness\:** Can the architecture support analytics, machine learning, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) where needed?
- **Delivery model\:** Will it deliver a working platform, documentation, knowledge transfer, and ongoing support?

Ask for two or three comparable client references and a clearly scoped proof of concept before committing to a large implementation.
